not_promoted.text: A CAT(0) cube complex is a simply connected complex of Euclidean unit cubes glued along faces, with flag vertex links and the induced Euclidean path metric. An isometric action of a discrete group G on a metric space X is proper here if, for one (equivalently every) x∈X and each R<∞, the set {g∈G:d(x,gx)≤R} is finite. It is cocompact if some compact K⊂X satisfies GK=X. A classical C′(1/6) presentation has finitely many generators and cyclically reduced relators, symmetrized by cyclic conjugation and inversion, such that any common initial word w of two distinct symmetrized relators has |w|<|r|/6 for each relator r containing it. Let G range over groups admitting such a presentation. Its virtual cubical dimension is inf{dim X : some finite-index subgroup H≤G acts properly by isometries on the finite-dimensional CAT(0) cube complex X}, with inf ∅=∞. Is there one finite integer D such that every such G has virtual cubical dimension at most D?
